protocol.title: Independent dependency-free-build full-stack implementation and maintenance study
protocol.description: A preregistered 96-session comparison of four unseen server-plus-browser assignments in Parley, Python, TypeScript, and Rust using parent-owned public evaluation and exact-build read-only validation.

validated_transport.channel: Two protected mode-0600 POSIX FIFOs carry bounded request and public-feedback messages; only the parent evaluator binds loopback.
validated_transport.threat_boundary: The transport is a measurement-integrity mechanism for command-constrained agents, not an isolation boundary against a deliberately hostile workspace process.

validated_exact_build_freeze.positive_control: Canonical manifest/lock survives native release and wasm32 release builds byte-for-byte.
validated_exact_build_freeze.negative_control: A displaced root block passes cargo metadata --locked --offline; cargo build --release returns zero and rewrites it; post-command hashes reject the build.
validated_exact_build_freeze.required_integration: Reference validation and measured evaluation must hash every protected/read-only input immediately after each exact build command for every language, in addition to final workspace integrity.

scratch_space_control.preflight_timing: Resolve disjoint work, journal, and attempt roots and require the full four-worker budget before journal initialization or any measured cell start.
scratch_space_control.evidence_boundary: The disposable work root and durable journal/attempt roots must be distinct real directories with no equal, ancestor, or descendant relationship.
scratch_space_control.cleanup_order: Persist the complete finished journal and external parent attempts before removing that journal's exact real immediate-child workspace through cleanup_finished_workspace.
scratch_space_control.resume_policy: On resume, seal every started unfinished cell as a permanent failure before reclaiming only workspaces certified by finished records; run only never-started cells.
scratch_space_control.failure_policy: Preflight, boundary, cleanup, or renewed capacity failure stops scheduling new cells, remains an execution-integrity failure after any cell starts, and never authorizes a rerun.
scratch_space_control.calibration_rule: Clean-room harness validation must measure peak per-cell scratch use. Revision 2 may increase, but never lower, the frozen reserve or per-worker budget before the first measured session.

matrix.derivation: 4 tasks x 4 languages x 2 agent configurations x 3 replicates

parley.stack: Generated native HTTP/JSON server with dependency-free strict typed-route codecs and generated browser WebAssembly bindings
parley.agent_context: Frozen 222-token v0.5.3 scaffold-aware card used alone and included in measured input tokens.

python.stack: FastAPI 0.141.1, Uvicorn 0.52.1, Pydantic 2.13.4, and a counted browser JavaScript application module

rust.stack: Axum 0.8.9, Tokio 1.53.1, Tower HTTP 0.7.0, Serde 1.0.229, serde_json 1.0.151, and a scalar WebAssembly export

scaffold_protocol.purpose: Supply stable language-appropriate transport, build, and browser wiring so the measured assignment is application implementation or repair rather than framework installation.
scaffold_protocol.editable: All task-specific application logic, typed request/response declarations, handlers, browser rule modules, and application manifests required by that language.
scaffold_protocol.read_only: Dependency locks, generic launch adapters, shared static shell, frozen contract, source printer, generated check client, public check wrapper, and benchmark configuration.
scaffold_protocol.source_visibility: The first shell command prints every editable and visibly read-only source/context file exactly once. Direct reconnaissance or reading protected case/configuration files is forbidden.
scaffold_protocol.dependency_setup: Pinned dependencies are installed or fetched before measured sessions. Each parent evaluation uses only the frozen local dependency store; network time is never part of a cell.
scaffold_protocol.reference_validation: Before any agent session, an isolated reference application for every task/language must run the exact measured build commands under post-command hash checks, preserve all protected/read-only inputs, and pass every public and hidden HTTP/browser case. Seeded maintenance applications must also build with stable hashes, fail at least one public semantic case, and pass after changing only the predeclared root file set.
scaffold_protocol.rust_lockfile: Generate Cargo.lock canonically from the final fullstack-agent-044 manifest. Run cargo build --locked --offline --release and the exact wasm32 release build under immediate post-command hash checks before the execution freeze, and preserve that reviewed hash in every measured workspace.
scaffold_protocol.symmetry: Every language receives the same English contract and semantic cases. Framework-specific source and configuration may differ, but no language receives a hidden expected value or repair.

session_protocol.runner: A new iteration-044 runner creates one isolated workspace, one external attempt directory, one immutable journal entry, and one ephemeral Codex thread per cell; it must not modify historical runners.
session_protocol.tool_policy: Disable user configuration, repository rules, plugins, apps, browser-use, computer-use, and multi-agent delegation. Use workspace-write with approval never and network disabled.
session_protocol.command_policy: The first shell command must be exactly ./sources and occur once. Every later shell command must be exactly ./check. At least one and at most twelve ./check commands are permitted.
session_protocol.public_feedback: Each ./check request is evaluated by the parent outside the sandbox. It records build output and exact public HTTP plus real-Chromium verdicts, then returns only bounded public feedback.
session_protocol.public_execution_requirement: Every completed public attempt must actually execute all four public cases, including the declared browser case. A build failure may short-circuit cases but remains a recorded failed attempt; zero semantic case execution cannot count as a passing check.
session_protocol.hidden_judgment: After the agent exits, the parent separately rebuilds the final source and executes all withheld HTTP/browser cases. Hidden inputs and values never enter the workspace or public transport.
session_protocol.attempt_capture: Preserve every parent-owned public attempt, source snapshot, file hash, changed-file list, command event, agent message, diagnostic, stdout/stderr, elapsed time, thread ID, and reported token count.
session_protocol.integrity: Hash all protected/read-only files immediately after every exact build and at cell finalization; reject unexpected files and symlinks; compare FIFO device/inode/type/mode/owner; revalidate frozen repository and toolchain provenance; require one start/finish journal record per cell; preserve the initial and renewed scratch checks without binding observed free bytes into resume identity; persist evidence and measured workspace bytes before bounded per-cell cleanup.
session_protocol.resume_policy: A started cell without a finished record becomes a permanent interruption failure; only never-started cells may execute.
session_protocol.failure_policy: Timeouts, interruptions, agent errors, nonzero exits, build failures, case failures, protocol violations, checker/FIFO/read-only integrity failures, missing source, unexpected files, scratch-boundary violations, low-space events after start, and cleanup failures are failures and remain in the complete result.

execution_freeze.description: Post-protocol harness, scratch lifecycle, v0.5.5 compact-context integration, and exact-build execution-integrity controls frozen before the first measured cell; task, case, model, metric, threshold, gate, compiler, context, and stack semantics are unchanged.
execution_freeze.public_attempt_storage: Atomic JSON files outside the agent workspace, revalidated during cell finalization and result aggregation.
execution_freeze.scratch_preflight: 17,179,869,184 bytes free required before journal initialization and every scheduling refill with work/journal/attempt roots proven disjoint; observed capacity is evidence rather than resume identity.
execution_freeze.workspace_cleanup: A separate immutable cleanup record is written only after the complete finished journal; it retains pre-cleanup workspace bytes and proves removal, absence, or a permanent cleanup failure.
execution_freeze.bounded_scheduler: At most four cells are active and no later cell is queued; a run-level capacity or cleanup failure stops refills and permanently journals all unstarted cells as failed without creating agent sessions.
execution_freeze.numeric_domain_guard: Identical parent-owned proxy for all languages; rejects only negative numeric values before forwarding other traffic.
execution_freeze.exact_build_integrity: Every protected/read-only file is checked before and immediately after each exact build command; any mutation fails the build and cell.
execution_freeze.resume_policy: A started cell without a finished record becomes a permanent interruption failure; finished evidence is reconciled with cleanup evidence; only never-started cells may execute.

metrics.correctness: Exact hidden HTTP status/JSON/error and real-browser scalar results, overall and by task, kind, language, model, and replicate.
metrics.first_check: Whether the first parent-owned public build and all four public cases pass, with HTTP and browser execution counts retained.
metrics.repairs: Number of later ./check attempts after the first, with every parent attempt retained outside the workspace.
metrics.tokens: Complete reported Codex input, cached input, uncached input, output, reasoning output, and input-plus-output totals. Primary efficiency uses complete input-plus-output tokens per assignment.
metrics.elapsed: Monotonic wall time for the whole fresh session, including parent-owned public builds and repairs but excluding dependency installation.
metrics.maintainability: Changed editable files, rough token edit size, and whether maintenance patches touch exactly the predeclared defect-root file set.
metrics.source: Final and seed UTF-8 bytes, physical lines, rough tokens, o200k_base tokens, and per-file SHA-256, reported descriptively rather than substituted for session tokens.
metrics.cross_target: HTTP/browser equality for the shared scalar contract plus explicit successful Chromium execution in public and hidden judgments.

primary_gate.execution_integrity: A preregistered scratch preflight must pass before journaling; all 96 cells must finish exactly once with unique thread IDs, exactly one journal start/finish, durable evidence before bounded workspace cleanup, intact repository/toolchain/checker/read-only/FIFO state including post-build hashes, compliant commands, required public HTTP/browser execution, no runner or cleanup error, and no selective rerun or exclusion.
primary_gate.correctness: Parley must pass 100% of hidden cases and its assignment success rate must be no lower than every baseline overall, within each agent configuration, and within implementation and maintenance tasks.
primary_gate.first_check: Parley's first-public-check assignment success rate must be no lower than the highest baseline rate overall and within each task kind.
primary_gate.tokens: Parley's median complete input-plus-output tokens per assignment must be no higher than the lowest baseline median overall and separately within each agent configuration.
primary_gate.elapsed: Parley's median elapsed seconds per assignment must be no higher than the lowest baseline median overall and separately within each agent configuration.
primary_gate.maintainability: Every hidden-correct Parley maintenance assignment must change exactly its predeclared root file set, and its exact-root rate must be no lower than every baseline.
primary_gate.verdict: All six conditions must hold for strict unseen full-stack agent parity/efficiency. Report every condition independently even when the overall gate fails.

secondary_analysis: Report full distributions, paired task/configuration/replicate cells, and per-task outcomes; do not replace the primary result with successful, repair-free, or model-selected subsets.
Report implementation and maintenance separately, including root-file quality, public/hidden HTTP-browser execution, and disagreement classes.
Report both model configurations separately before any pooled interpretation.
Report public-attempt counts and public case executions so a build-only or browser-skipped check cannot be mistaken for semantic feedback.
Report post-build protected/read-only hash checks by language and build phase; do not collapse them into only the final workspace flag.
Report scratch preflight, peak per-cell/worker usage, each evidence-gated cleanup, and final free space; never delete durable evidence to improve a result.
Compare studies 036–043 only as motivation and mechanism history. Do not combine their task results, tokens, or timing with 044.
Classify failures after preserving the frozen outcome; classification cannot change a verdict.
interpretation_boundary: The study covers four small synthetic server-plus-browser contracts, two model IDs, one reasoning setting, and one frozen toolchain environment.
Stack scaffolds test application work, not greenfield framework discovery, dependency selection, deployment, sustained load, authentication, databases, accessibility, or production operations.
Framework source and compiler implementations are infrastructure. Their application-facing context is preserved, while complete session tokens remain the primary cost.
A deterministic scalar ES-module export exercised in real Chromium is a cross-target behavior check, not a general user-interface evaluation.
Synthetic maintenance defects measure the declared boundary behaviors and do not estimate the distribution of production defects.
Even a fully passing gate cannot prove universal language superiority; it supports only the frozen comparative claim.
A failed strict gate remains useful evidence and cannot be repaired by same-corpus language, context, prompt, task, runner, threshold, or metric tuning.
protocol.implementation_rule: Scaffolds, reference applications, dependency preparation, and the runner are implemented only after this protocol commit. Their exact hashes and clean-room reference evidence must be committed in a final pre-measurement execution freeze. No measured session may start before that checkpoint.
protocol.change_rule: From corpus commit cef46dcdf70183e2c64e235bf9699184ba166eb5 onward, no task, case, expected value, language semantics, compiler, context, metric, threshold, model, reasoning setting, replicate count, or primary gate may change based on scaffolds, reference code, validation, smoke checks, or measured output. An objective harness defect may be corrected only before measured execution in a documented zero-session amendment preserving old commits and semantic hashes. Scratch calibration may only increase the preregistered budget before the first measured session.
protocol.stop_rule: Run every frozen cell once, preserve and publish the complete result whether positive, mixed, negative, or invalid, and make no same-corpus optimization or rerun. Any later language or product change requires an independently frozen corpus outside iteration 044.

logic.par.text:
to seismic_array_score with short_sensors as number, deep_sensors as number, relay_towers as number, ash_warning as yesno giving number:
    let short be short_sensors times 12
    let deep be deep_sensors times 20
    let ash be 0
    if ash_warning:
        set ash to relay_towers times 7
    let required be short plus deep plus ash
    let capacity be relay_towers times 48
    let processed be required
    if processed is more than capacity:
        set processed to capacity
    let backlogged be required minus capacity
    if backlogged is less than 0:
        set backlogged to 0
    let rounds be number from (required divided by 37)
    give back processed plus (backlogged times 6) plus (rounds times 10)

main.par.text:
include "logic.par"
a seismic_request has short_sensors as number, deep_sensors as number, relay_towers as number, ash_warning as yesno
a seismic_response has sensor_total as number, short_scan_seconds as number, deep_scan_seconds as number, ash_sync_seconds as number, array_required_seconds as number, relay_capacity_seconds as number, processed_seconds as number, backlogged_seconds as number, scan_rounds as number, array_score as number, array_state as text
a service_status has service as text, ready as yesno
to project_status giving service_status:
    give back a service_status with service "Seismic Array", ready yes
to handle_request with request as seismic_request giving seismic_response:
    let short be request's short_sensors times 12
    let deep be request's deep_sensors times 20
    let ash be 0
    if request's ash_warning:
        set ash to request's relay_towers times 7
    let required be short plus deep plus ash
    let capacity be request's relay_towers times 48
    let processed be required
    if processed is more than capacity:
        set processed to capacity
    let backlogged be required minus capacity
    if backlogged is less than 0:
        set backlogged to 0
    let rounds be number from (required divided by 37)
    let state be "aligned"
    if backlogged is more than 0:
        set state to "routine_backlog"
        if request's ash_warning:
            set state to "ash_backlog"
    give back a seismic_response with sensor_total (request's short_sensors plus request's deep_sensors), short_scan_seconds short, deep_scan_seconds deep, ash_sync_seconds ash, array_required_seconds required, relay_capacity_seconds capacity, processed_seconds processed, backlogged_seconds backlogged, scan_rounds rounds, array_score (seismic_array_score with request's short_sensors, request's deep_sensors, request's relay_towers, request's ash_warning), array_state state

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Build a seismic sensor array planner across HTTP and browser targets

Implement the frozen Seismic Array contract in the supplied stack. sensor_total is short_sensors + deep_sensors. short_scan_seconds is short_sensors * 12. deep_scan_seconds is deep_sensors * 20. ash_sync_seconds is relay_towers * 7 during an ash_warning and zero otherwise. array_required_seconds is short_scan_seconds + deep_scan_seconds + ash_sync_seconds. relay_capacity_seconds is relay_towers * 48. processed_seconds is min(array_required_seconds, relay_capacity_seconds). backlogged_seconds is max(array_required_seconds - relay_capacity_seconds, 0). scan_rounds is array_required_seconds divided by 37 using floor division. array_score is processed_seconds + backlogged_seconds * 6 + scan_rounds * 10. array_state is aligned when backlogged_seconds is zero, ash_backlog when backlog remains during an ash warning, and routine_backlog otherwise. The browser export returns array_score.

## HTTP

- `GET /status/seismic-array-ready` returns `{"service":"Seismic Array","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v8/seismic-array` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `short_sensors`: number
- `deep_sensors`: number
- `relay_towers`: number
- `ash_warning`: yesno

Response fields:

- `sensor_total`: number
- `short_scan_seconds`: number
- `deep_scan_seconds`: number
- `ash_sync_seconds`: number
- `array_required_seconds`: number
- `relay_capacity_seconds`: number
- `processed_seconds`: number
- `backlogged_seconds`: number
- `scan_rounds`: number
- `array_score`: number
- `array_state`: text

## Browser

Export `seismic_array_score` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`array_score` for equivalent inputs.

a seismic_response has sensor_total as number, short_scan_seconds as number, deep_scan_seconds as number, ash_sync_seconds as number, array_required_seconds as number, relay_capacity_seconds as number, processed_seconds as number, backlogged_seconds as number, scan_rounds as number, array_score as number, array_state as text
a service_status has service as text, ready as yesno
to project_status giving service_status:
    give back a service_status with service "Seismic Array", ready yes
to handle_request with request as seismic_request giving seismic_response:
    let short be request's short_sensors times 12
    let deep be request's deep_sensors times 20
    let ash be 0
    if request's ash_warning:
        set ash to request's relay_towers times 7
    let required be short plus deep plus ash
    let capacity be request's relay_towers times 48
    let processed be required
    if processed is more than capacity:
        set processed to capacity
    let backlogged be required minus capacity
    if backlogged is less than 0:
        set backlogged to 0
    let rounds be number from (required divided by 37)
    let state be "aligned"
    if backlogged is more than 0:
        set state to "routine_backlog"
        if request's ash_warning:
            set state to "ash_backlog"
    give back a seismic_response with sensor_total (request's short_sensors plus request's deep_sensors), short_scan_seconds short, deep_scan_seconds deep, ash_sync_seconds ash, array_required_seconds required, relay_capacity_seconds capacity, processed_seconds processed, backlogged_seconds backlogged, scan_rounds rounds, array_score (seismic_array_score with request's short_sensors, request's deep_sensors, request's relay_towers, request's ash_warning), array_state state

logic.par.text:
to museum_conservation_score with canvas_crates as number, textile_crates as number, work_tables as number, emergency_drying as yesno giving number:
    let canvas be canvas_crates times 9
    let textile be textile_crates times 15
    let drying be 0
    if emergency_drying:
        set drying to work_tables times 6
    let required be canvas plus textile plus drying
    let capacity be work_tables times 43
    let completed be required
    if completed is more than capacity:
        set completed to capacity
    let deferred be required minus capacity
    if deferred is less than 0:
        set deferred to 0
    let rounds be number from (required divided by 34)
    give back completed plus (deferred times 7) plus (rounds times 11)

# Build a museum conservation scheduler across HTTP and browser targets

Implement the frozen Museum Conservation contract in the supplied stack. crate_total is canvas_crates + textile_crates. canvas_work_minutes is canvas_crates * 9. textile_work_minutes is textile_crates * 15. drying_setup_minutes is work_tables * 6 during emergency_drying and zero otherwise. conservation_required_minutes is canvas_work_minutes + textile_work_minutes + drying_setup_minutes. table_capacity_minutes is work_tables * 43. completed_minutes is min(conservation_required_minutes, table_capacity_minutes). deferred_minutes is max(conservation_required_minutes - table_capacity_minutes, 0). conservation_rounds is conservation_required_minutes divided by 34 using floor division. conservation_score is completed_minutes + deferred_minutes * 7 + conservation_rounds * 11. conservation_state is preserved when deferred_minutes is zero, emergency_queue when delay remains during emergency drying, and routine_queue otherwise. The browser export returns conservation_score.

## HTTP

- `GET /status/museum-conservation-ready` returns `{"service":"Museum Conservation","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v8/museum-conservation` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `canvas_crates`: number
- `textile_crates`: number
- `work_tables`: number
- `emergency_drying`: yesno

Response fields:

- `crate_total`: number
- `canvas_work_minutes`: number
- `textile_work_minutes`: number
- `drying_setup_minutes`: number
- `conservation_required_minutes`: number
- `table_capacity_minutes`: number
- `completed_minutes`: number
- `deferred_minutes`: number
- `conservation_rounds`: number
- `conservation_score`: number
- `conservation_state`: text

Export `museum_conservation_score` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`conservation_score` for equivalent inputs.

logic.par.text:
to museum_conservation_score with canvas_crates as number, textile_crates as number, work_tables as number, emergency_drying as yesno giving number:
    let canvas be canvas_crates times 9
    let textile be textile_crates times 15
    let drying be 0
    if emergency_drying:
        set drying to work_tables times 6
    let required be canvas plus textile plus drying
    let capacity be work_tables times 43
    let completed be required
    if completed is more than capacity:
        set completed to capacity
    let deferred be required minus capacity
    if deferred is less than 0:
        set deferred to 0
    let rounds be number from (required divided by 34)
    give back completed plus deferred times 7 plus rounds times 11

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Build a museum conservation scheduler across HTTP and browser targets

Implement the frozen Museum Conservation contract in the supplied stack. crate_total is canvas_crates + textile_crates. canvas_work_minutes is canvas_crates * 9. textile_work_minutes is textile_crates * 15. drying_setup_minutes is work_tables * 6 during emergency_drying and zero otherwise. conservation_required_minutes is canvas_work_minutes + textile_work_minutes + drying_setup_minutes. table_capacity_minutes is work_tables * 43. completed_minutes is min(conservation_required_minutes, table_capacity_minutes). deferred_minutes is max(conservation_required_minutes - table_capacity_minutes, 0). conservation_rounds is conservation_required_minutes divided by 34 using floor division. conservation_score is completed_minutes + deferred_minutes * 7 + conservation_rounds * 11. conservation_state is preserved when deferred_minutes is zero, emergency_queue when delay remains during emergency drying, and routine_queue otherwise. The browser export returns conservation_score.

## HTTP

- `GET /status/museum-conservation-ready` returns `{"service":"Museum Conservation","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v8/museum-conservation` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `canvas_crates`: number
- `textile_crates`: number
- `work_tables`: number
- `emergency_drying`: yesno

Response fields:

- `crate_total`: number
- `canvas_work_minutes`: number
- `textile_work_minutes`: number
- `drying_setup_minutes`: number
- `conservation_required_minutes`: number
- `table_capacity_minutes`: number
- `completed_minutes`: number
- `deferred_minutes`: number
- `conservation_rounds`: number
- `conservation_score`: number
- `conservation_state`: text

## Browser

Export `museum_conservation_score` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`conservation_score` for equivalent inputs.

Repair the supplied Canal Lock application. barge_total is freight_barges + tour_barges. freight_lock_units is freight_barges * 10. tour_lock_units is tour_barges * 17. flood_lock_units is lock_chambers * 8 during flood_protocol and zero otherwise. lock_required_units is freight_lock_units + tour_lock_units + flood_lock_units. lock_capacity_units is lock_chambers * 45. passed_lock_units is min(lock_required_units, lock_capacity_units). held_lock_units is max(lock_required_units - lock_capacity_units, 0). clearance_units is max(lock_capacity_units - passed_lock_units, 0). canal_state is clear when held_lock_units is zero, flood_hold when load remains during flood protocol, and routine_hold otherwise. The HTTP response and browser export must use the same rule; the browser export returns clearance_units.

## HTTP

- `GET /status/canal-lock-ready` returns `{"service":"Canal Lock","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v8/canal-lock` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `freight_barges`: number
- `tour_barges`: number
- `lock_chambers`: number
- `flood_protocol`: yesno

Response fields:

- `barge_total`: number
- `freight_lock_units`: number
- `tour_lock_units`: number
- `flood_lock_units`: number
- `lock_required_units`: number
- `lock_capacity_units`: number
- `passed_lock_units`: number
- `held_lock_units`: number
- `clearance_units`: number
- `canal_state`: text

## Browser

Export `canal_clearance_units` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`clearance_units` for equivalent inputs.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse, JSONResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from pydantic import ValidationError

from logic import RequestInput, handle

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 16_384
PUBLIC = Path(__file__).with_name("public")

def error(code: str, status: int, detail: str) -> JSONResponse:
    return JSONResponse({"error": code, "detail": detail}, status_code=status)

app = FastAPI(docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None)

@app.get("/status/canal-lock-ready")
async def status() -> dict[str, object]:
    return {"service": "Canal Lock", "ready": True}

@app.post("/api/v8/canal-lock")
async def endpoint(request: Request) -> JSONResponse:
    content_type = request.headers.get("content-type", "").split(";", 1)[0].strip().lower()
    if content_type != "application/json" and not content_type.endswith("+json"):
        return error("json_content_type_required", 415, "expected application/json")
    declared = request.headers.get("content-length")
    if declared and (not declared.isdigit() or int(declared) > MAX_BODY_BYTES):
        return error("body_too_large", 413, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes")
    body = await request.body()
    if len(body) > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
        return error("body_too_large", 413, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes")
    try:
        value = json.loads(body)
        parsed = RequestInput.model_validate(value, strict=True)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValidationError) as exc:
        return error("invalid_json", 400, str(exc))
    return JSONResponse(handle(parsed))

@app.api_route("/api/{rest:path}", methods=["GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE"])
async def missing_api(rest: str) -> JSONResponse:
    return error("not_found", 404, f"no API route /api/{rest}")

@app.get("/parley.js")
async def browser_module() -> FileResponse:
    return FileResponse(Path(__file__).with_name("browser.js"), media_type="text/javascript")

app.mount("/", StaticFiles(directory=PUBLIC, html=True), name="public")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=int(os.environ["PARLEY_WEB_PORT"]), log_level="warning")

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Repair a heating-cycle divisor in a thermal greenhouse

Repair the supplied Thermal Greenhouse application. row_total is seedling_rows + fruit_rows. seedling_heat_units is seedling_rows * 8. fruit_heat_units is fruit_rows * 14. frost_heat_units is heat_pumps * 5 during frost_cycle and zero otherwise. heat_required_units is seedling_heat_units + fruit_heat_units + frost_heat_units. pump_capacity_units is heat_pumps * 41. delivered_heat_units is min(heat_required_units, pump_capacity_units). heat_deficit_units is max(heat_required_units - pump_capacity_units, 0). heat_reserve_units is max(pump_capacity_units - delivered_heat_units, 0). heating_cycles is heat_required_units divided by 29 using floor division. greenhouse_score is delivered_heat_units + heat_deficit_units * 5 + heating_cycles * 7. greenhouse_state is balanced when heat_deficit_units is zero, frost_shortage when a deficit remains during a frost cycle, and heat_shortage otherwise. The HTTP response and browser export must use the same rule; the browser export returns greenhouse_score.

## HTTP

- `GET /status/thermal-greenhouse-ready` returns `{"service":"Thermal Greenhouse","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v8/thermal-greenhouse` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `seedling_rows`: number
- `fruit_rows`: number
- `heat_pumps`: number
- `frost_cycle`: yesno

Response fields:

- `row_total`: number
- `seedling_heat_units`: number
- `fruit_heat_units`: number
- `frost_heat_units`: number
- `heat_required_units`: number
- `pump_capacity_units`: number
- `delivered_heat_units`: number
- `heat_deficit_units`: number
- `heat_reserve_units`: number
- `heating_cycles`: number
- `greenhouse_score`: number
- `greenhouse_state`: text

## Browser

Export `thermal_greenhouse_score` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`greenhouse_score` for equivalent inputs.

use std::env;
use axum::{Router, body::{Body, to_bytes}, extract::Request, http::{StatusCode, header}, response::{IntoResponse, Response}, routing::{any, get, post}};
use fullstack_agent_044::{RequestInput, handle};
use serde::Serialize;
use serde_json::json;
use tower_http::services::{ServeDir, ServeFile};

const MAX_BODY_BYTES: usize = 16_384;
const BROWSER_MODULE: &str = r#"const asI64 = (value, name) => { if (typeof value === "bigint") return value; if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value)) throw new TypeError(`${name} must be a safe whole number`); return BigInt(value); };
export async function loadParley() {
  const response = await fetch(new URL("/fullstack_agent_044.wasm", import.meta.url));
  const result = await WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(response);
  const wasm = result.instance.exports;
  return { thermal_greenhouse_score: (a, b, c, d) => wasm.parley_thermal_greenhouse_score(asI64(a, 'a'), asI64(b, 'b'), asI64(c, 'c'), d ? 1 : 0) };
}"#;
fn json_response(value: impl Serialize, status: StatusCode) -> Response { let mut response = (status, serde_json::to_vec(&value).unwrap()).into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("application/json")); response }
fn error(code: &str, status: StatusCode, detail: impl Into<String>) -> Response { json_response(json!({"error": code, "detail": detail.into()}), status) }
async fn status() -> Response { json_response(json!({"service": "Thermal Greenhouse", "ready": true}), StatusCode::OK) }
async fn endpoint(request: Request) -> Response {
    let media_type = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_TYPE).and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok()).unwrap_or("").split(';').next().unwrap_or("").trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    if media_type != "application/json" && !media_type.ends_with("+json") { return error("json_content_type_required", StatusCode::UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, "expected application/json"); }
    if let Some(length) = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_LENGTH) { let declared = length.to_str().ok().and_then(|value| value.parse::<usize>().ok()); if declared.is_none_or(|value| value > MAX_BODY_BYTES) { return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes"); } }
    let body = match to_bytes(request.into_body(), MAX_BODY_BYTES).await { Ok(body) => body, Err(_) => return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes") };
    match serde_json::from_slice::<RequestInput>(&body) { Ok(value) if value.valid() => json_response(handle(value), StatusCode::OK), Ok(_) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "numeric value outside contract"), Err(reason) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, reason.to_string()) }
}
async fn missing_api(request: Request<Body>) -> Response { error("not_found", StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, format!("no API route {}", request.uri().path())) }
async fn browser_module() -> Response { let mut response = BROWSER_MODULE.into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("text/javascript; charset=utf-8")); response }
#[tokio::main] async fn main() {
    let wasm = env::var_os("FULLSTACK_044_WASM").map(std::path::PathBuf::from).unwrap();
    let app = Router::new().route("/status/thermal-greenhouse-ready", get(status)).route("/api/v8/thermal-greenhouse", post(endpoint)).route("/api/{*rest}", any(missing_api)).route("/parley.js", get(browser_module)).route_service("/fullstack_agent_044.wasm", ServeFile::new(wasm)).fallback_service(ServeDir::new("public").append_index_html_on_directories(true));
    let port = env::var("PARLEY_WEB_PORT").unwrap().parse::<u16>().unwrap();
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", port)).await.unwrap(); axum::serve(listener, app).await.unwrap();
}

# Repair a heating-cycle divisor in a thermal greenhouse

Repair the supplied Thermal Greenhouse application. row_total is seedling_rows + fruit_rows. seedling_heat_units is seedling_rows * 8. fruit_heat_units is fruit_rows * 14. frost_heat_units is heat_pumps * 5 during frost_cycle and zero otherwise. heat_required_units is seedling_heat_units + fruit_heat_units + frost_heat_units. pump_capacity_units is heat_pumps * 41. delivered_heat_units is min(heat_required_units, pump_capacity_units). heat_deficit_units is max(heat_required_units - pump_capacity_units, 0). heat_reserve_units is max(pump_capacity_units - delivered_heat_units, 0). heating_cycles is heat_required_units divided by 29 using floor division. greenhouse_score is delivered_heat_units + heat_deficit_units * 5 + heating_cycles * 7. greenhouse_state is balanced when heat_deficit_units is zero, frost_shortage when a deficit remains during a frost cycle, and heat_shortage otherwise. The HTTP response and browser export must use the same rule; the browser export returns greenhouse_score.

## HTTP

- `GET /status/thermal-greenhouse-ready` returns `{"service":"Thermal Greenhouse","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v8/thermal-greenhouse` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `seedling_rows`: number
- `fruit_rows`: number
- `heat_pumps`: number
- `frost_cycle`: yesno

Response fields:

- `row_total`: number
- `seedling_heat_units`: number
- `fruit_heat_units`: number
- `frost_heat_units`: number
- `heat_required_units`: number
- `pump_capacity_units`: number
- `delivered_heat_units`: number
- `heat_deficit_units`: number
- `heat_reserve_units`: number
- `heating_cycles`: number
- `greenhouse_score`: number
- `greenhouse_state`: text

## Browser

Export `thermal_greenhouse_score` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`greenhouse_score` for equivalent inputs.

use std::env;
use axum::{Router, body::{Body, to_bytes}, extract::Request, http::{StatusCode, header}, response::{IntoResponse, Response}, routing::{any, get, post}};
use fullstack_agent_044::{RequestInput, handle};
use serde::Serialize;
use serde_json::json;
use tower_http::services::{ServeDir, ServeFile};

const MAX_BODY_BYTES: usize = 16_384;
const BROWSER_MODULE: &str = r#"const asI64 = (value, name) => { if (typeof value === "bigint") return value; if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value)) throw new TypeError(`${name} must be a safe whole number`); return BigInt(value); };
export async function loadParley() {
  const response = await fetch(new URL("/fullstack_agent_044.wasm", import.meta.url));
  const result = await WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(response);
  const wasm = result.instance.exports;
  return { thermal_greenhouse_score: (a, b, c, d) => wasm.parley_thermal_greenhouse_score(asI64(a, 'a'), asI64(b, 'b'), asI64(c, 'c'), d ? 1 : 0) };
}"#;
fn json_response(value: impl Serialize, status: StatusCode) -> Response { let mut response = (status, serde_json::to_vec(&value).unwrap()).into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("application/json")); response }
fn error(code: &str, status: StatusCode, detail: impl Into<String>) -> Response { json_response(json!({"error": code, "detail": detail.into()}), status) }
async fn status() -> Response { json_response(json!({"service": "Thermal Greenhouse", "ready": true}), StatusCode::OK) }
async fn endpoint(request: Request) -> Response {
    let media_type = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_TYPE).and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok()).unwrap_or("").split(';').next().unwrap_or("").trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    if media_type != "application/json" && !media_type.ends_with("+json") { return error("json_content_type_required", StatusCode::UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, "expected application/json"); }

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Build a museum conservation scheduler across HTTP and browser targets

Implement the frozen Museum Conservation contract in the supplied stack. crate_total is canvas_crates + textile_crates. canvas_work_minutes is canvas_crates * 9. textile_work_minutes is textile_crates * 15. drying_setup_minutes is work_tables * 6 during emergency_drying and zero otherwise. conservation_required_minutes is canvas_work_minutes + textile_work_minutes + drying_setup_minutes. table_capacity_minutes is work_tables * 43. completed_minutes is min(conservation_required_minutes, table_capacity_minutes). deferred_minutes is max(conservation_required_minutes - table_capacity_minutes, 0). conservation_rounds is conservation_required_minutes divided by 34 using floor division. conservation_score is completed_minutes + deferred_minutes * 7 + conservation_rounds * 11. conservation_state is preserved when deferred_minutes is zero, emergency_queue when delay remains during emergency drying, and routine_queue otherwise. The browser export returns conservation_score.

## HTTP

- `GET /status/museum-conservation-ready` returns `{"service":"Museum Conservation","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v8/museum-conservation` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `canvas_crates`: number
- `textile_crates`: number
- `work_tables`: number
- `emergency_drying`: yesno

Response fields:

- `crate_total`: number
- `canvas_work_minutes`: number
- `textile_work_minutes`: number
- `drying_setup_minutes`: number
- `conservation_required_minutes`: number
- `table_capacity_minutes`: number
- `completed_minutes`: number
- `deferred_minutes`: number
- `conservation_rounds`: number
- `conservation_score`: number
- `conservation_state`: text

## Browser

Export `museum_conservation_score` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field

use std::env;
use axum::{Router, body::{Body, to_bytes}, extract::Request, http::{StatusCode, header}, response::{IntoResponse, Response}, routing::{any, get, post}};
use fullstack_agent_044::{RequestInput, handle};
use serde::Serialize;
use serde_json::json;
use tower_http::services::{ServeDir, ServeFile};

const MAX_BODY_BYTES: usize = 16_384;
const BROWSER_MODULE: &str = r#"const asI64 = (value, name) => { if (typeof value === "bigint") return value; if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value)) throw new TypeError(`${name} must be a safe whole number`); return BigInt(value); };
export async function loadParley() {
  const response = await fetch(new URL("/fullstack_agent_044.wasm", import.meta.url));
  const result = await WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(response);
  const wasm = result.instance.exports;
  return { museum_conservation_score: (a, b, c, d) => wasm.parley_museum_conservation_score(asI64(a, 'a'), asI64(b, 'b'), asI64(c, 'c'), d ? 1 : 0) };
}"#;
fn json_response(value: impl Serialize, status: StatusCode) -> Response { let mut response = (status, serde_json::to_vec(&value).unwrap()).into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("application/json")); response }
fn error(code: &str, status: StatusCode, detail: impl Into<String>) -> Response { json_response(json!({"error": code, "detail": detail.into()}), status) }
async fn status() -> Response { json_response(json!({"service": "Museum Conservation", "ready": true}), StatusCode::OK) }
async fn endpoint(request: Request) -> Response {
    let media_type = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_TYPE).and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok()).unwrap_or("").split(';').next().unwrap_or("").trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    if media_type != "application/json" && !media_type.ends_with("+json") { return error("json_content_type_required", StatusCode::UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, "expected application/json"); }
    if let Some(length) = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_LENGTH) { let declared = length.to_str().ok().and_then(|value| value.parse::<usize>().ok()); if declared.is_none_or(|value| value > MAX_BODY_BYTES) { return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes"); } }
    let body = match to_bytes(request.into_body(), MAX_BODY_BYTES).await { Ok(body) => body, Err(_) => return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes") };
    match serde_json::from_slice::<RequestInput>(&body) { Ok(value) if value.valid() => json_response(handle(value), StatusCode::OK), Ok(_) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "numeric value outside contract"), Err(reason) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, reason.to_string()) }
}
async fn missing_api(request: Request<Body>) -> Response { error("not_found", StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, format!("no API route {}", request.uri().path())) }
async fn browser_module() -> Response { let mut response = BROWSER_MODULE.into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("text/javascript; charset=utf-8")); response }
#[tokio::main] async fn main() {
    let wasm = env::var_os("FULLSTACK_044_WASM").map(std::path::PathBuf::from).unwrap();
    let app = Router::new().route("/status/museum-conservation-ready", get(status)).route("/api/v8/museum-conservation", post(endpoint)).route("/api/{*rest}", any(missing_api)).route("/parley.js", get(browser_module)).route_service("/fullstack_agent_044.wasm", ServeFile::new(wasm)).fallback_service(ServeDir::new("public").append_index_html_on_directories(true));
    let port = env::var("PARLEY_WEB_PORT").unwrap().parse::<u16>().unwrap();
    let listener = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind(("127.0.0.1", port)).await.unwrap(); axum::serve(listener, app).await.unwrap();
}

# Build a museum conservation scheduler across HTTP and browser targets

Implement the frozen Museum Conservation contract in the supplied stack. crate_total is canvas_crates + textile_crates. canvas_work_minutes is canvas_crates * 9. textile_work_minutes is textile_crates * 15. drying_setup_minutes is work_tables * 6 during emergency_drying and zero otherwise. conservation_required_minutes is canvas_work_minutes + textile_work_minutes + drying_setup_minutes. table_capacity_minutes is work_tables * 43. completed_minutes is min(conservation_required_minutes, table_capacity_minutes). deferred_minutes is max(conservation_required_minutes - table_capacity_minutes, 0). conservation_rounds is conservation_required_minutes divided by 34 using floor division. conservation_score is completed_minutes + deferred_minutes * 7 + conservation_rounds * 11. conservation_state is preserved when deferred_minutes is zero, emergency_queue when delay remains during emergency drying, and routine_queue otherwise. The browser export returns conservation_score.

## HTTP

- `GET /status/museum-conservation-ready` returns `{"service":"Museum Conservation","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v8/museum-conservation` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `canvas_crates`: number
- `textile_crates`: number
- `work_tables`: number
- `emergency_drying`: yesno

Response fields:

- `crate_total`: number
- `canvas_work_minutes`: number
- `textile_work_minutes`: number
- `drying_setup_minutes`: number
- `conservation_required_minutes`: number
- `table_capacity_minutes`: number
- `completed_minutes`: number
- `deferred_minutes`: number
- `conservation_rounds`: number
- `conservation_score`: number
- `conservation_state`: text

## Browser

Export `museum_conservation_score` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`conservation_score` for equivalent inputs.

use std::env;
use axum::{Router, body::{Body, to_bytes}, extract::Request, http::{StatusCode, header}, response::{IntoResponse, Response}, routing::{any, get, post}};
use fullstack_agent_044::{RequestInput, handle};
use serde::Serialize;
use serde_json::json;
use tower_http::services::{ServeDir, ServeFile};

const MAX_BODY_BYTES: usize = 16_384;
const BROWSER_MODULE: &str = r#"const asI64 = (value, name) => { if (typeof value === "bigint") return value; if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value)) throw new TypeError(`${name} must be a safe whole number`); return BigInt(value); };
export async function loadParley() {
  const response = await fetch(new URL("/fullstack_agent_044.wasm", import.meta.url));
  const result = await WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(response);
  const wasm = result.instance.exports;
  return { museum_conservation_score: (a, b, c, d) => wasm.parley_museum_conservation_score(asI64(a, 'a'), asI64(b, 'b'), asI64(c, 'c'), d ? 1 : 0) };
}"#;
fn json_response(value: impl Serialize, status: StatusCode) -> Response { let mut response = (status, serde_json::to_vec(&value).unwrap()).into_response(); response.headers_mut().insert(header::CONTENT_TYPE, header::HeaderValue::from_static("application/json")); response }
fn error(code: &str, status: StatusCode, detail: impl Into<String>) -> Response { json_response(json!({"error": code, "detail": detail.into()}), status) }
async fn status() -> Response { json_response(json!({"service": "Museum Conservation", "ready": true}), StatusCode::OK) }
async fn endpoint(request: Request) -> Response {
    let media_type = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_TYPE).and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok()).unwrap_or("").split(';').next().unwrap_or("").trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
    if media_type != "application/json" && !media_type.ends_with("+json") { return error("json_content_type_required", StatusCode::UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, "expected application/json"); }
    if let Some(length) = request.headers().get(header::CONTENT_LENGTH) { let declared = length.to_str().ok().and_then(|value| value.parse::<usize>().ok()); if declared.is_none_or(|value| value > MAX_BODY_BYTES) { return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes"); } }
    let body = match to_bytes(request.into_body(), MAX_BODY_BYTES).await { Ok(body) => body, Err(_) => return error("body_too_large", StatusCode::PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes") };
    match serde_json::from_slice::<RequestInput>(&body) { Ok(value) if value.valid() => json_response(handle(value), StatusCode::OK), Ok(_) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, "numeric value outside contract"), Err(reason) => error("invalid_json", StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, reason.to_string()) }

to seismic_array_score with short_sensors as number, deep_sensors as number, relay_towers as number, ash_warning as yesno giving number:
    let short be short_sensors times 12
    let deep be deep_sensors times 20
    let ash be 0
    if ash_warning:
        set ash to relay_towers times 7
    let required be short plus deep plus ash
    let capacity be relay_towers times 48
    let processed be required
    if processed is more than capacity:
        set processed to capacity
    let backlogged be required minus capacity
    if backlogged is less than 0:
        set backlogged to 0
    let rounds be number from (required divided by 37)
    give back processed plus (backlogged times 6) plus (rounds times 10)

# Build a seismic sensor array planner across HTTP and browser targets

Implement the frozen Seismic Array contract in the supplied stack. sensor_total is short_sensors + deep_sensors. short_scan_seconds is short_sensors * 12. deep_scan_seconds is deep_sensors * 20. ash_sync_seconds is relay_towers * 7 during an ash_warning and zero otherwise. array_required_seconds is short_scan_seconds + deep_scan_seconds + ash_sync_seconds. relay_capacity_seconds is relay_towers * 48. processed_seconds is min(array_required_seconds, relay_capacity_seconds). backlogged_seconds is max(array_required_seconds - relay_capacity_seconds, 0). scan_rounds is array_required_seconds divided by 37 using floor division. array_score is processed_seconds + backlogged_seconds * 6 + scan_rounds * 10. array_state is aligned when backlogged_seconds is zero, ash_backlog when backlog remains during an ash warning, and routine_backlog otherwise. The browser export returns array_score.

## HTTP

- `GET /status/seismic-array-ready` returns `{"service":"Seismic Array","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v8/seismic-array` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `short_sensors`: number
- `deep_sensors`: number
- `relay_towers`: number
- `ash_warning`: yesno

Response fields:

- `sensor_total`: number
- `short_scan_seconds`: number
- `deep_scan_seconds`: number
- `ash_sync_seconds`: number
- `array_required_seconds`: number
- `relay_capacity_seconds`: number
- `processed_seconds`: number
- `backlogged_seconds`: number
- `scan_rounds`: number
- `array_score`: number
- `array_state`: text

## Browser

Export `seismic_array_score` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`array_score` for equivalent inputs.

- `GET /status/seismic-array-ready` returns `{"service":"Seismic Array","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v8/seismic-array` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `short_sensors`: number
- `deep_sensors`: number
- `relay_towers`: number
- `ash_warning`: yesno

Response fields:

- `sensor_total`: number
- `short_scan_seconds`: number
- `deep_scan_seconds`: number
- `ash_sync_seconds`: number
- `array_required_seconds`: number
- `relay_capacity_seconds`: number
- `processed_seconds`: number
- `backlogged_seconds`: number
- `scan_rounds`: number
- `array_score`: number
- `array_state`: text

## Browser

Export `seismic_array_score` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`array_score` for equivalent inputs.

include "logic.par"
a seismic_request has short_sensors as number, deep_sensors as number, relay_towers as number, ash_warning as yesno
a seismic_response has sensor_total as number, short_scan_seconds as number, deep_scan_seconds as number, ash_sync_seconds as number, array_required_seconds as number, relay_capacity_seconds as number, processed_seconds as number, backlogged_seconds as number, scan_rounds as number, array_score as number, array_state as text
a service_status has service as text, ready as yesno
to project_status giving service_status:

to handle_request with request as seismic_request giving seismic_response:
    let short be request's short_sensors times 12
    let deep be request's deep_sensors times 20
    let ash be 0
    if request's ash_warning:
        set ash to request's relay_towers times 7
    let required be short plus deep plus ash
    let capacity be request's relay_towers times 48
    let processed be required
    if processed is more than capacity:
        set processed to capacity
    let backlogged be required minus capacity
    if backlogged is less than 0:
        set backlogged to 0
    let rounds be number from (required divided by 37)
    let state be "aligned"
    if backlogged is more than 0:
        set state to "routine_backlog"
        if request's ash_warning:
            set state to "ash_backlog"
    give back a seismic_response with sensor_total (request's short_sensors plus request's deep_sensors), short_scan_seconds short, deep_scan_seconds deep, ash_sync_seconds ash, array_required_seconds required, relay_capacity_seconds capacity, processed_seconds processed, backlogged_seconds backlogged, scan_rounds rounds, array_score (seismic_array_score with request's short_sensors, request's deep_sensors, request's relay_towers, request's ash_warning), array_state state

to museum_conservation_score with canvas_crates as number, textile_crates as number, work_tables as number, emergency_drying as yesno giving number:
    let drying_setup_minutes be 0
    if emergency_drying:
        set drying_setup_minutes to work_tables times 6
    let conservation_required_minutes be (canvas_crates times 9) plus (textile_crates times 15) plus drying_setup_minutes
    let table_capacity_minutes be work_tables times 43
    let completed_minutes be conservation_required_minutes
    if completed_minutes is more than table_capacity_minutes:
        set completed_minutes to table_capacity_minutes
    let deferred_minutes be conservation_required_minutes minus table_capacity_minutes
    if deferred_minutes is less than 0:
        set deferred_minutes to 0
    let conservation_rounds be number from (conservation_required_minutes divided by 34)
    give back completed_minutes plus (deferred_minutes times 7) plus (conservation_rounds times 11)

# Build a museum conservation scheduler across HTTP and browser targets

Implement the frozen Museum Conservation contract in the supplied stack. crate_total is canvas_crates + textile_crates. canvas_work_minutes is canvas_crates * 9. textile_work_minutes is textile_crates * 15. drying_setup_minutes is work_tables * 6 during emergency_drying and zero otherwise. conservation_required_minutes is canvas_work_minutes + textile_work_minutes + drying_setup_minutes. table_capacity_minutes is work_tables * 43. completed_minutes is min(conservation_required_minutes, table_capacity_minutes). deferred_minutes is max(conservation_required_minutes - table_capacity_minutes, 0). conservation_rounds is conservation_required_minutes divided by 34 using floor division. conservation_score is completed_minutes + deferred_minutes * 7 + conservation_rounds * 11. conservation_state is preserved when deferred_minutes is zero, emergency_queue when delay remains during emergency drying, and routine_queue otherwise. The browser export returns conservation_score.

- `GET /status/museum-conservation-ready` returns `{"service":"Museum Conservation","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v8/museum-conservation` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `canvas_crates`: number
- `textile_crates`: number
- `work_tables`: number
- `emergency_drying`: yesno

- `conservation_required_minutes`: number
- `table_capacity_minutes`: number

- `conservation_rounds`: number
- `conservation_score`: number
- `conservation_state`: text

Export `museum_conservation_score` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`conservation_score` for equivalent inputs.

logic.par.text:
to museum_conservation_score with canvas_crates as number, textile_crates as number, work_tables as number, emergency_drying as yesno giving number:
    let canvas be canvas_crates times 9
    let textile be textile_crates times 15
    let drying be 0
    if emergency_drying:
        set drying to work_tables times 6
    let required be canvas plus textile plus drying
    let capacity be work_tables times 43
    let completed be required
    if completed is more than capacity:
        set completed to capacity
    let deferred be required minus capacity
    if deferred is less than 0:
        set deferred to 0
    let rounds be number from (required divided by 34)
    give back completed plus (deferred times 7) plus (rounds times 11)

include "logic.par"
a conservation_request has canvas_crates as number, textile_crates as number, work_tables as number, emergency_drying as yesno
a conservation_response has crate_total as number, canvas_work_minutes as number, textile_work_minutes as number, drying_setup_minutes as number, conservation_required_minutes as number, table_capacity_minutes as number, completed_minutes as number, deferred_minutes as number, conservation_rounds as number, conservation_score as number, conservation_state as text

to project_status giving service_status:
    give back a service_status with service "Museum Conservation", ready yes

    let drying be 0
    if request's emergency_drying:
        set drying to request's work_tables times 6
    let required be canvas plus textile plus drying
    let capacity be request's work_tables times 43
    let completed be required
    if completed is more than capacity:
        set completed to capacity
    let deferred be required minus capacity
    if deferred is less than 0:
        set deferred to 0
    let rounds be number from (required divided by 34)
    let state be "preserved"
    if deferred is more than 0:
        set state to "routine_queue"
        if request's emergency_drying:
            set state to "emergency_queue"
    give back a conservation_response with crate_total (request's canvas_crates plus request's textile_crates), canvas_work_minutes canvas, textile_work_minutes textile, drying_setup_minutes drying, conservation_required_minutes required, table_capacity_minutes capacity, completed_minutes completed, deferred_minutes deferred, conservation_rounds rounds, conservation_score (museum_conservation_score with request's canvas_crates, request's textile_crates, request's work_tables, request's emergency_drying), conservation_state state

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Build a museum conservation scheduler across HTTP and browser targets

Implement the frozen Museum Conservation contract in the supplied stack. crate_total is canvas_crates + textile_crates. canvas_work_minutes is canvas_crates * 9. textile_work_minutes is textile_crates * 15. drying_setup_minutes is work_tables * 6 during emergency_drying and zero otherwise. conservation_required_minutes is canvas_work_minutes + textile_work_minutes + drying_setup_minutes. table_capacity_minutes is work_tables * 43. completed_minutes is min(conservation_required_minutes, table_capacity_minutes). deferred_minutes is max(conservation_required_minutes - table_capacity_minutes, 0). conservation_rounds is conservation_required_minutes divided by 34 using floor division. conservation_score is completed_minutes + deferred_minutes * 7 + conservation_rounds * 11. conservation_state is preserved when deferred_minutes is zero, emergency_queue when delay remains during emergency drying, and routine_queue otherwise. The browser export returns conservation_score.

## HTTP

- `GET /status/museum-conservation-ready` returns `{"service":"Museum Conservation","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v8/museum-conservation` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `canvas_crates`: number
- `textile_crates`: number
- `work_tables`: number
- `emergency_drying`: yesno

Response fields:

- `crate_total`: number
- `canvas_work_minutes`: number
- `textile_work_minutes`: number
- `drying_setup_minutes`: number
- `conservation_required_minutes`: number
- `table_capacity_minutes`: number
- `completed_minutes`: number
- `deferred_minutes`: number
- `conservation_rounds`: number
- `conservation_score`: number
- `conservation_state`: text

## Browser

Export `museum_conservation_score` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`conservation_score` for equivalent inputs.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse, JSONResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from pydantic import ValidationError

from logic import RequestInput, handle

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 16_384
PUBLIC = Path(__file__).with_name("public")

def error(code: str, status: int, detail: str) -> JSONResponse:
    return JSONResponse({"error": code, "detail": detail}, status_code=status)

app = FastAPI(docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None)

@app.get("/status/museum-conservation-ready")
async def status() -> dict[str, object]:
    return {"service": "Museum Conservation", "ready": True}

@app.post("/api/v8/museum-conservation")
async def endpoint(request: Request) -> JSONResponse:
    content_type = request.headers.get("content-type", "").split(";", 1)[0].strip().lower()
    if content_type != "application/json" and not content_type.endswith("+json"):
        return error("json_content_type_required", 415, "expected application/json")
    declared = request.headers.get("content-length")
    if declared and (not declared.isdigit() or int(declared) > MAX_BODY_BYTES):
        return error("body_too_large", 413, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes")
    body = await request.body()
    if len(body) > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
        return error("body_too_large", 413, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes")
    try:
        value = json.loads(body)
        parsed = RequestInput.model_validate(value, strict=True)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValidationError) as exc:
        return error("invalid_json", 400, str(exc))
    return JSONResponse(handle(parsed))

@app.api_route("/api/{rest:path}", methods=["GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE"])
async def missing_api(rest: str) -> JSONResponse:
    return error("not_found", 404, f"no API route /api/{rest}")

@app.get("/parley.js")
async def browser_module() -> FileResponse:
    return FileResponse(Path(__file__).with_name("browser.js"), media_type="text/javascript")

app.mount("/", StaticFiles(directory=PUBLIC, html=True), name="public")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=int(os.environ["PARLEY_WEB_PORT"]), log_level="warning")

# Repair a heating-cycle divisor in a thermal greenhouse

Repair the supplied Thermal Greenhouse application. row_total is seedling_rows + fruit_rows. seedling_heat_units is seedling_rows * 8. fruit_heat_units is fruit_rows * 14. frost_heat_units is heat_pumps * 5 during frost_cycle and zero otherwise. heat_required_units is seedling_heat_units + fruit_heat_units + frost_heat_units. pump_capacity_units is heat_pumps * 41. delivered_heat_units is min(heat_required_units, pump_capacity_units). heat_deficit_units is max(heat_required_units - pump_capacity_units, 0). heat_reserve_units is max(pump_capacity_units - delivered_heat_units, 0). heating_cycles is heat_required_units divided by 29 using floor division. greenhouse_score is delivered_heat_units + heat_deficit_units * 5 + heating_cycles * 7. greenhouse_state is balanced when heat_deficit_units is zero, frost_shortage when a deficit remains during a frost cycle, and heat_shortage otherwise. The HTTP response and browser export must use the same rule; the browser export returns greenhouse_score.

## HTTP

- `GET /status/thermal-greenhouse-ready` returns `{"service":"Thermal Greenhouse","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v8/thermal-greenhouse` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `seedling_rows`: number
- `fruit_rows`: number
- `heat_pumps`: number
- `frost_cycle`: yesno

Response fields:

- `row_total`: number
- `seedling_heat_units`: number
- `fruit_heat_units`: number
- `frost_heat_units`: number
- `heat_required_units`: number
- `pump_capacity_units`: number
- `delivered_heat_units`: number
- `heat_deficit_units`: number
- `heat_reserve_units`: number
- `heating_cycles`: number
- `greenhouse_score`: number
- `greenhouse_state`: text

## Browser

Export `thermal_greenhouse_score` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`greenhouse_score` for equivalent inputs.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse, JSONResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from pydantic import ValidationError

from logic import RequestInput, handle

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 16_384
PUBLIC = Path(__file__).with_name("public")

def error(code: str, status: int, detail: str) -> JSONResponse:
    return JSONResponse({"error": code, "detail": detail}, status_code=status)

app = FastAPI(docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None)

@app.get("/status/thermal-greenhouse-ready")
async def status() -> dict[str, object]:
    return {"service": "Thermal Greenhouse", "ready": True}

@app.post("/api/v8/thermal-greenhouse")
async def endpoint(request: Request) -> JSONResponse:
    content_type = request.headers.get("content-type", "").split(";", 1)[0].strip().lower()
    if content_type != "application/json" and not content_type.endswith("+json"):
        return error("json_content_type_required", 415, "expected application/json")
    declared = request.headers.get("content-length")
    if declared and (not declared.isdigit() or int(declared) > MAX_BODY_BYTES):
        return error("body_too_large", 413, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes")
    body = await request.body()
    if len(body) > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
        return error("body_too_large", 413, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes")
    try:
        value = json.loads(body)
        parsed = RequestInput.model_validate(value, strict=True)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValidationError) as exc:
        return error("invalid_json", 400, str(exc))
    return JSONResponse(handle(parsed))

@app.api_route("/api/{rest:path}", methods=["GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE"])
async def missing_api(rest: str) -> JSONResponse:
    return error("not_found", 404, f"no API route /api/{rest}")

@app.get("/parley.js")
async def browser_module() -> FileResponse:
    return FileResponse(Path(__file__).with_name("browser.js"), media_type="text/javascript")

app.mount("/", StaticFiles(directory=PUBLIC, html=True), name="public")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=int(os.environ["PARLEY_WEB_PORT"]), log_level="warning")

===== CONTRACT.md [read-only] =====
# Build a museum conservation scheduler across HTTP and browser targets

Implement the frozen Museum Conservation contract in the supplied stack. crate_total is canvas_crates + textile_crates. canvas_work_minutes is canvas_crates * 9. textile_work_minutes is textile_crates * 15. drying_setup_minutes is work_tables * 6 during emergency_drying and zero otherwise. conservation_required_minutes is canvas_work_minutes + textile_work_minutes + drying_setup_minutes. table_capacity_minutes is work_tables * 43. completed_minutes is min(conservation_required_minutes, table_capacity_minutes). deferred_minutes is max(conservation_required_minutes - table_capacity_minutes, 0). conservation_rounds is conservation_required_minutes divided by 34 using floor division. conservation_score is completed_minutes + deferred_minutes * 7 + conservation_rounds * 11. conservation_state is preserved when deferred_minutes is zero, emergency_queue when delay remains during emergency drying, and routine_queue otherwise. The browser export returns conservation_score.

## HTTP

- `GET /status/museum-conservation-ready` returns `{"service":"Museum Conservation","ready":true}`.
- `POST /api/v8/museum-conservation` accepts strict JSON and returns strict JSON.
- A number is a nonnegative JSON integer and never a boolean.
- Unknown, missing, wrongly typed, or out-of-domain fields return
  status 400 with error `invalid_json`.
- A non-JSON POST returns 415 with error `json_content_type_required`.
- A body over 16384 bytes returns 413 with error `body_too_large`.

Request fields:

- `canvas_crates`: number
- `textile_crates`: number
- `work_tables`: number
- `emergency_drying`: yesno

Response fields:

- `crate_total`: number
- `canvas_work_minutes`: number
- `textile_work_minutes`: number
- `drying_setup_minutes`: number
- `conservation_required_minutes`: number
- `table_capacity_minutes`: number
- `completed_minutes`: number
- `deferred_minutes`: number
- `conservation_rounds`: number
- `conservation_score`: number
- `conservation_state`: text

## Browser

Export `museum_conservation_score` with request fields in the order listed
above. It returns the same value as response field
`conservation_score` for equivalent inputs.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse, JSONResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from pydantic import ValidationError

from logic import RequestInput, handle

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 16_384
PUBLIC = Path(__file__).with_name("public")

def error(code: str, status: int, detail: str) -> JSONResponse:
    return JSONResponse({"error": code, "detail": detail}, status_code=status)

app = FastAPI(docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None)

@app.get("/status/museum-conservation-ready")
async def status() -> dict[str, object]:
    return {"service": "Museum Conservation", "ready": True}

@app.post("/api/v8/museum-conservation")
async def endpoint(request: Request) -> JSONResponse:
    content_type = request.headers.get("content-type", "").split(";", 1)[0].strip().lower()
    if content_type != "application/json" and not content_type.endswith("+json"):
        return error("json_content_type_required", 415, "expected application/json")
    declared = request.headers.get("content-length")
    if declared and (not declared.isdigit() or int(declared) > MAX_BODY_BYTES):
        return error("body_too_large", 413, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes")
    body = await request.body()
    if len(body) > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
        return error("body_too_large", 413, "request body exceeds 16384 bytes")
    try:
        value = json.loads(body)
        parsed = RequestInput.model_validate(value, strict=True)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, ValidationError) as exc:
        return error("invalid_json", 400, str(exc))
    return JSONResponse(handle(parsed))

@app.api_route("/api/{rest:path}", methods=["GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE"])
async def missing_api(rest: str) -> JSONResponse:
    return error("not_found", 404, f"no API route /api/{rest}")

@app.get("/parley.js")
async def browser_module() -> FileResponse:
    return FileResponse(Path(__file__).with_name("browser.js"), media_type="text/javascript")

app.mount("/", StaticFiles(directory=PUBLIC, html=True), name="public")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=int(os.environ["PARLEY_WEB_PORT"]), log_level="warning")
